notes: The same entity as Home Assistant 2026.10.4 sends it with unit_system us_customary: foreca.json's values fed to Home Assistant's WeatherEntity as native values in the units its attributes state (°C, hPa, km/h, km, mm), state and forecasts read back through the weather component with hass.config.units set to US_CUSTOMARY_SYSTEM. Temperatures come back as whole °F (ints: outside °C the weather entity rounds to whole degrees), pressure in inHg, wind in mph, visibility in mi and precipitation in in, each to 2 decimals; humidity, bearings, conditions, datetimes and every other field are as in the metric file. The metric file's notes follow; their numbers are metric. The test does not freeze the clock, so now is the first hourly entry. Daily datetimes are local midnight in Home Assistant's time zone (the test runs in US/Pacific, hence -07:00), while hourly ones carry the station's own offset (+03:00). Changes for realism (test-data artefacts): the test's daily mock starts the day after its hourly and current data, while Foreca's daily list starts today, so daily is moved back one day (local midnight in Home Assistant's zone, still -07:00). Its second day was 'snowy' at 12/4 C in Helsinki in early September; it is 'rainy' (0.4 mm) instead.
